text:
maya: Heads up — canary for horizon-liteq-v3 is showing a spike in structured-output parse failures for func calls (int8 build). 5.2% parse error rate this morning vs 0.4% on fp32.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy horizon-liteq-v3 (canary=10%) started by @maya at 2026-03-21T08:00:00Z :rocket:

oncall-bot: Alert: parse_failure_rate > 1% for route /invoke/horizon-liteq-v3 (canary) — threshold breached

maya: sample malformed output (redacted):
```
{"action": "create_ticket", "args": {"title": "Payment error", "metadata": {"user_id": 12345},}

}
```

alex: ugh trailing comma + stray newline in middle of object. looks like tokenization + kv-cache boundary issue to me.

sam: are we sure it's only int8? can we run a parity mirror (float vs int8) on the same request set to diff exact token streams?

maya: good call. kicked off parity job `canary/546789/parity-run` with 2k sample prompts (same seeds).

katie: suggestion: enable soft-json-coercion postprocess on the canary only — it trims trailing commas and tries to repair simple malforms. low-risk guardrail while we investigate.

alex: also consider lowering continuous-batching window for the canary to avoid interleaved kv-prefixes. set batch_window_ms=5 for canary.

maya: sam — parity run results: int8 parse errors 5.1%, fp32 0.3%. diffs show suffix noise concentrated where responses include nested arrays and code fences.

sam: can you paste an example diff?

maya: pasted:
```
FP32:
{"action":"exec","args":[{"id":1,"cmd":"ls"}]}

INT8:
{"action":"exec","args":[{"id":1,"cmd":"ls"}],

}
```

katie: that's classic suffix drop + extra newline then comma. If kv-cache truncates and model regresses to emitting an extra token, it can leave a hanging comma when array close gets delayed.

devex: quick mitigation we can flip on: 1) soft-json-coercion, 2) retry-on-parse with 1 incremental backoff and enforce max_retries=1 for canary requests, 3) enable postprocess-snapshotting for failed parses to S3 for offline stitching. Want me to roll a canary patch?

maya: yes please. roll soft-json + retry 1 for only the canary for 2 hours. we'll monitor parse_rate and false-positive repairs.

deploy-bot: Patch roll (canary-sanitizer) queued by @devex — target: horizon-liteq-v3/canary.

sam: experiments to run next:
- run token-level diff of kv-cache boundaries between fp32+int8
- replicate with kv-cache disabled for int8 to see if failure drops
- test with quantization-aware tokenizer mapping (we've seen token-split shifts)

alex: also add a small eval suite: 300 prompts with nested arrays/code blocks and assert JSON schema compliance; measure per-prompt token-level alignment score.

maya: agreed. owned by @sam and @alex. i'll keep an eye on dashboard — https://console.redwood.ai/canary/546789 (metrics updated)

katie: if repairs spike and downstream apps see hallucinated args, we should set a hard fail for canary instead of auto-repair. watch for increased downstream errors.

maya: noted. if downstream error > 0.2% after repair, we'll abort canary.

oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Will re-alert if parse_failure_rate > 2% or downstream_error > 0.2%.

maya: TL;DR: int8 canary shows parse regressions concentrated at suffixes, mitigation = soft-json-coercion + single retry + lower batch window. follow-ups: parity token-diff + kv-cache toggle + schema-eval harness.

alex: I'll start the token-diff job and post results here.

sam: I'll run kv-cache-off replicate later today.

katie: i'll draft a short note for support explaining temporary soft-repair behavior so they can triage customer reports. :memo: 

maya: thanks all.
